newsitem.title: NORWAY: DnB profits from strong Norway economy.
newsitem.headline: DnB profits from strong Norway economy.

text.p: Den norske Bank ASA (DNB), Norway's biggest commercial bank, on Tuesday booked 1996 net profits of 2.70 billion crowns ($408.1 million), 1.7 percent higher than in 1995.
The bank attributed the result partly to the strong Norwegian economy.
The profits corresponded to earnings per share of 4.22 crowns and a 20 percent return on equity, DnB said in a statement.
The board of directors proposed a dividend of 1.75 crowns per share, up from 1.5 crowns in 1995.
"The strong results reflect sound operations, reduced costs and a healthy trend in the Norwegian economy," group managing director Finn Hvistendahl said in a statement accompanying the results.

"The positive developments in DnB's core operations have led to growth in lending and deposits which has almost compensated for the pressure on interest margins. This has coincided with a favourable loan-loss trend and continued reversals on prevous loan losses," he said.
Net interest income, the bank's core business, fell to 4.24 billion crowns from 4.35 billion. Other operating income also dropped, to 2.67 billion from 2.77 billion crowns.
Narrowing interest margins have put pressure on Norwegian banks to increase profits from other than net interest income.
Net reversals on loans, guarantees -- or writebacks on bad loans turned good -- fell to 380 million crowns from 479 million.
The volume of new loan losses was 837 million crowns in 1996, down from 1.25 billion in the previous year.

"Loan loss developments have been favourable in all sectors, apart from shipping, due to the general improvement in customer's financial position and the increase in the value of collateral," DnB said.
Operating profits came to 2.72 billion crowns, up 61 million from 1995. Pre-tax profits before loan losses were 2.34 billion crowns, compared with 2.20 billion crowns the year before.
The result included 56 million crowns in income from insurance company Vital Forsikring, which was acquired by DnB from 1996.
